gen-fs-kola-satoshi: Bold and blunt is not quite right, so call Kola distinctive: a plain display face with a thin-stroke-free build. Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and a wide e, every stroke cut to one width, built for steady text.
gen-fs-kola-switzer: Kola's plain, bold display letters grab attention first. Switzer takes over where reading begins, its wire-like, tubular strokes and tall waist line holding up as plain sans text.
gen-fs-kola-work-sans: Distinctive from the first glance, Kola stays plain and confident. Work Sans adds a contemporary sans with tips that never creep toward touching, and that clarity is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-abeezee: Wiry, technical, almost shouting in capital-sized lowercase. ABeeZee works underneath as a sans with neon-tube thickness, so give it generous size to let those open terminals breathe.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-alexandria: Alexandria reads clean and tall-bodied, with wide open terminals and short stems above and below. And Nippo sits over it with wire-cut strokes of unvarying thickness, so the page gets a technical headline and a smooth sans-serif text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-amiko: Technical and contemporary, Nippo draws every stroke like cut wire with no hairlines anywhere. Amiko answers in a modern sans-serif with chunky crayon-tall lowercase and terminals that flare outward like tongs.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-bangla: Nippo's small letters stand proud, nearly capital-sized, in strokes that look cut from wire. And Anek Bangla gives that a counterpart, a plain sans with wide s curves and a short run to the ascender.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-devanagari: Wire-cut and technical, all upright. Anek Devanagari follows with distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone, so a sans-serif text sits comfortably beneath Nippo's swelling-free curves.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati opens with lowercase that rivals the capitals and a gaping c, all in a clean plain sans. Anek Gujarati then reads easily, because nothing in it fights Nippo's pencil-like, unvarying heading lines.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Nippo's lowercase stands nearly capital-sized, drawn like wire. Nippo handles the hairline-free, technical headline work, while Anek Gurmukhi's big open counters and generous round characters keep the sans-serif text clean.
